To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Docker containers deployed on NVMe SSDs have 2x higher performance than on SATA SSDs, and the performance can be further improved up to 1.5x by using the optimized configuration of Docker storage options.

Docker containers on NVMe SSDs have a significant performance improvement over the legacy SATA SSDs and the default Docker configuration options for SSD deployments do not provide the best possible performance.

Docker on high performance SSD storage has the following characteristics: (1) Docker on SSD storage has a much higher throughput and lower latency compared to Docker on HDD, (2) the performance of Docker on SSD storage is highly sensitive to the configuration of the storage driver, and (3) Docker on SSD has a higher throughput and lower tail latency compared to the native file system.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the default configuration of Docker on a Linux host system is sufficient to utilize the full potential of high performance SSDs, but there is a significant room for performance improvement with the proper configuration.
Docker containers are not well-suited for high performance SSDs, but with some careful tuning and configuration, they can be made to work well with them.
Docker on NVMe SSDs provides the most consistent and best performance, while Docker on SATA SSDs and HDDs provides the least consistent and worst performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in order to fully utilize the high performance of NVMe-based SSDs, the Docker containers should use the raw block device directly, and the storage driver for the Docker container should be set as either overlay2 or devicemapper.

the Docker storage drivers have significant impact on performance of containerized application and the choice of Docker storage drivers can be optimized for different application workloads.

, the performance of the Docker containers on SSDs is heavily impacted by the underlying block layer.
the default Docker deployment options do not provide the best performance on high speed SSDs.
